d:
Take this waterskin and journey deep into the emerald shade o' Ashenvale. Astranaar rests cradled by waters untouched by corruption. Ruins litter the bed o' the lake, hinting at a bygone era. Bring back a sample from the lake. Pure, ancient, and possibly enchanted water.
It's the last liquid I need before I send ye back to Norric.
Board the boat in Menethil to Auberdine. It stops in Southshore on the way over.
And mind yerself... The forest's got eyes, and they don't blink.
p: Do you have the water yet, friend? If ye haven't made the trek to Kalimdor yet, be careful.
c: Well done, friend! With all three samples in hand, I'll brew ye a vial o' water so pure it'd make the mountains weep. It's the final piece for yer rite o' passage. I'm proud to call ye kin, friend. Ye've done adventurer proud, and I look forward to hearing yer tales in the future.

d: Norric will have one more task for ye before rewarding ye with the water totem rites. The vial of water I've given ye is necessary for whatever that task is. Go now and find him. We shall meet again some day.
p:
Hello again, friend. Yer looking well.
What brings you back to me so soon?
c:
Ahh, water blessed by Hervdana herself, and gathered by your own hands? A gift indeed.
These vials shall birth your sapta, letting you glimpse the water spirits at Stendel's Pond, near Moonbrook. The last few drops of the water have an equally important purpose... Waste not even a cork stopper dampened with sacred water.

d:
In Westfall, outside o' Moonbrook lies Stendel's Pond. Once a pure spring, now touched by dark forces. The spirits there 'ave gone silent.
Ye must face the corruption that fouls the waters. Take its bracers and the last drops o' Hervdana's potion, then place 'em on the shrine. That'll call forth a spirit, cleansed and true. Speak with it, learn what ye can.
Bring me proof the deed's done, and I'll grant ye the totem.
p: The shrine stands aged and forgotten, cloaked in dust and cobwebs. The pond beside it lies eerily still, its surface untouched by wind or life. Scattered along the shore are the bones of beasts once burdened by labor. The water's murky sheen raises a troubling question--has it been poisoned by the surrounding malaise, or is it the very source of it?
c: You place the bracers atop the shrine and then pour the remaining drops of Norric's potion into dry stone. You begin to incant the simple words Norric taught you and the droplets vaporize atop the stone within the bindings....

d: Light erupts as the final word leaves your lips. The hiss of water turning to mist fades into silence, and your senses reel as the corrupt spirits around you unravel, their essence scattered like ash in the wind.
c:
Thanks to you. Thanks to the adventurers.
Corruption ebbs but life continues to wane. Up to adventurers to protect life.

d:
Take shard. Take shard and give life.
Give life and understand. Understand water is life... Corruption stops life.
You protect and give life with water's power.
p: How fared your journey to Westfall? Success there is hard to measure, but even small victories carry weight.
c:
Aye, this is the proof I asked for, and ye've done well, friend. I'm proud to be the first to offer my congratulations--and yer water totem. Use it wisely, and may fortune walk beside ye.
Yer next trial won't come soon, so take this time to learn. Pure water heals, aye, but its gifts go far beyond mending wounds.

d:
The turncoat clearly was afraid of what the cult had planned, enough so to defect and seek our aid. It's truly unfortunate that he is dead and took his secrets to the grave with him.
We must discuss this further to determine our next steps.
c:
We could try and send peacekeepers to directly engage the cult forces, but we would not fare well against them in open battle.
We are going to need a different approach.
